report.summary: Chunk 1 of 6 of daedalus/structcore/clones.py: module docstring, imports, normalize_source, _normalize_python, _strip_comments_generic. Claims about clone detection strategies and comment stripping logic are partially checkable.
risks: _strip_comments_generic | medium | Unterminated literal handling stops at newline, but if quote char appears inside a string literal (e.g., Python triple-quote) the logic may prematurely close the string. The code does not handle multi-character delimiters like '''. | Check if spec.string_delims can contain multi-character strings and if the code correctly handles them.
todos: Verify that _strip_comments_generic correctly handles multi-character string delimiters (e.g., Python triple quotes) as the current single-char quote comparison may fail.

handoff.purpose: Module introduction, imports, and core normalization/comments-stripping functions for clone detection.

symbols.note: Public entry point for source normalization; dispatches to Python-specific or generic normalizer.

symbols.note: Normalizes Python source using tokenize; drops comments, newlines, indentation, and block docstrings.

symbols.name: _strip_comments_generic
symbols.note: Generic comment stripper that is string-literal aware; handles line/block comments per LanguageSpec.

claims.text: unit_clusters — precise, function/method level. Normalizes each unit (strip comments/docstrings/whitespace) and SHA1-fingerprints it; identical fingerprints across >=2 sites are a clone cluster. Catches Type-1/2 exact and renamed-literal clones.
claims.why: The function unit_clusters is not defined in this chunk; only normalize_source and comment stripping are present. The claim about its behavior cannot be verified.

claims.text: window_clusters — universal, needs no parser. Slides an N-line window of normalized source across every file and finds identical runs shared by >=2 files. Catches copy-paste across files in ANY language/text.
claims.why: The function window_clusters is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Every cluster is safety-annotated: if any site lives in a SAFETY-CLASS path it is flagged do_not_collapse (the HV-triplication lesson) and never recommended for merge.
claims.why: No code in this chunk implements safety annotation or references SAFETY-CLASS paths.

claims.why: Reference to codemap is outside this chunk; the tokenize path is implemented as _normalize_python but its equivalence to codemap is uncheckable.

claims.why: No previous implementation is present in this chunk; the claim about historical behavior cannot be verified.

claims.text: Two confirmed cases: send("SOUR:VOLT // 500"); -> send("SOUR:VOLT and send("SOUR:VOLT // 50"); -> send("SOUR:VOLT (identical!)
claims.why: No code in this chunk reproduces those cases; it's a historical anecdote.

claims.text: a /* inside a string, where the old block regex ran with re.S and swallowed everything up to the next */ — deleting whole function bodies and merging unrelated functions into one cluster.
claims.why: No old implementation is present; current code handles strings verbatim.

claims.text: Single left-to-right pass, because the three states are mutually exclusive: inside a string, comment markers are text; outside one, a quote opens a string.
claims.why: The while loop with i < n iterates left-to-right, and the logic distinguishes string vs non-string state.

claims.text: Which quotes open a string is per-language (spec.string_delims): Rust's 'a is a lifetime, not a literal, and consuming to the next ' would eat the code the old version was already eating.
claims.why: The code uses spec.string_delims but does not show how it is set; the Rust example is outside the chunk.

claims.text: Unterminated literals stop at end-of-line rather than running to EOF, so a stray quote degrades one line instead of the rest of the file.
claims.why: Inside the string copy loop, when encountering '\n' the code breaks out of the inner while loop, stopping at end-of-line.

observations.what: The module docstring describes two functions (unit_clusters, window_clusters) that are not present in this chunk; they appear only as claims about future or external code.
normalize_source dispatches to _normalize_python for Python and _normalize_generic for others; _normalize_generic is imported but not defined in this chunk.
_strip_comments_generic handles single-character string delimiters only; multi-character delimiters (e.g., Python ''' or """) are not supported, potentially causing incorrect behavior.

The string copy loop uses 'if c == ch' to close the literal; this does not account for escaped quotes within the string (e.g., '\"' in Python). However, the loop does handle backslash-escaped characters by skipping the next character, so escaped quotes are correctly not treated as closing delimiters.

The comment stripping does not handle block comments (e.g., /* */) in the generic case; the code only checks for line comment markers. The docstring mentions spec.block_comment but it is not used in the shown portion.
The function _strip_comments_generic is cut off mid-implementation; the block comment handling may appear later in the chunk but is not visible here.
